## Summary

Icarus fails to elaborate a sampled-value function in a procedural event control when the module declares a default clocking block. IEEE 1800-2017 §16.9.3 permits sampled-value functions in procedural code and infers the default clocking event outside assertions. The default clocking support umbrella issue #17 explicitly left default clocking out of scope.

## Minimal reproducer

```systemverilog
module top;
  logic clk_tb = 0;
  logic signal = 0;
  always #5 clk_tb = ~clk_tb;
  default clocking default_clk @(posedge clk_tb); endclocking
  initial begin
    #2 signal = 1;
    #10 $finish;
  end
  initial forever @($changed(signal)) $display("changed at %0t", $time);
endmodule
```

Compile with `iverilog -g2017 -gassertions -s top default-clocking-changed.sv -o test.vvp`.

## Observed

Pinned Icarus 9b5fad2afb4104caa816b257d5bccc40f01b8c66 (binary SHA-256 `6cd9749cb1e981820f64fdc737ae458bf6c46e3fcad8927afaf92649ee9a3288`) and current main ca559fd97b19bd6a56cc10f0faf8583b4077975f (binary SHA-256 `c99ee9c08468fb20f7635fb3380adb0d620c9037c19c02236a435a61c7be0130`) both fail with `System function $ivl_clocking_sample not defined in system table or SFT file(s)`.

The same behavior is present in five event controls in Caliptra's SoC-IFC testbench. A testbench overlay that samples `$changed` at `@(posedge clk_tb)` compiles and runs, and SoC-IFC row 21 passes with that overlay. Verilator 5.032 does not validate the original form: with timing enabled it reports an internal `Unknown node type ... STABLE` error.

## Expected

Support sampled-value function expressions in procedural event controls using the inferred default clocking event, or emit a direct unsupported-feature diagnostic instead of the unresolved internal system function. Preserve the LRM sampling region semantics.

## Evidence

Reproducer, compiler output, and the passing workaround are retained under `evidence/caliptra-bfm-m17-20261019/diagnostics/socifc-clocking-sample/`.

A class method declared as an extern function without an explicit return type, then defined out of class, is rejected by the pinned Icarus build. The equivalent source is accepted by Verilator 5.032. Adding an explicit `void` return type makes both tools accept it.

```systemverilog
package p;
  class C;
    extern function lock_fuses();
  endclass
  function C::lock_fuses();
  endfunction
endpackage
module top;
  import p::*;
  initial begin C c = new(); c.lock_fuses(); end
```

## Summary

Icarus c339 leaves an enum member at its zero value in a packed-struct assignment pattern when another member is assigned an expression wider than that member. In the reproducer, `rd_wr_en` stays `RW_IDLE` although the pattern explicitly assigns `RW_READ`.

## Minimal reproducer

[Self-contained SystemVerilog test](https://github.com/QD-EDA/qd-bfm/blob/61b1e83/evidence/caliptra-bfm-environment-matrix-20261011/reproducers/icarus-struct-assignment-width/self-contained.sv)

The type is:

```systemverilog
typedef enum logic [1:0] {RW_IDLE = 2'b00, RW_READ = 2'b01} mode_t;
typedef struct packed { mode_t rd_wr_en; logic [13:0] addr; } mem_if_t;
```

The failing assignment is `bad <= '{rd_wr_en: RW_READ, addr: locked_src_addr + num_mem_operands};`, where the address operands are 14 and 32 bits. The control assignment explicitly sized to 14 bits produces the expected packed value.

## Observed

With Icarus source revision `c339b9f2287a743aeb7ab6de6528e8d34a4dd602`:

```text
bad=0002 bad_en=00 bad_addr=0002
```

The sized control gives `good=4002 good_en=01 good_addr=0002`. Verilator 5.051 produces `bad=4002 bad_en=01`, matching the control. Logs and binary hashes are in the linked evidence directory.

This also affects the pinned Adams Bridge `sigencode_z_top.sv`: request assignment patterns combine the `RW_READ` control field with a 32-bit counter expression assigned to a 14-bit address member. Its testbench then reports 3,584 mismatches with unknown outputs and no output-memory writes.

IEEE 1800-2017 §10.9.2 says assignment-pattern member expressions are evaluated in the context of the corresponding member type: https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf

Related closed issues #19 and #41 cover broader struct/pattern work and struct defaults, but I did not find this member-context-sizing behavior described there.
title: Packed struct assignment pattern member loses enum value with wider sibling expression

## Measurement

A pinned Caliptra top-level run on Icarus c339 progressed from trace cycle 100 to 25,700 before its 3,500-second guard expired. That is 25,600 cycles over 3,500 seconds, or 7.31 effective cycles per wall-second. The wall duration is from the whole firmware runner, including setup, so this is a conservative end-to-end rate rather than a VVP-only rate.

The current Caliptra test matrix contains 271 active YAML rows. ## Gap

The compiler accepts `output` and `inout` as covergroup constructor formals. IEEE 1800-2017 and IEEE 1800-2023 §19.3 require both directions to be illegal for a covergroup formal. Legal `input` and `ref` formals must remain accepted; `ref` is read-only and tracks the actual variable for sampling.

## Reproducer

Run each declaration separately in strict `-g2017` and `-g2023` mode:

```systemverilog
module t;
  int value;
  covergroup cg(output int arg);
    cp: coverpoint arg;
  endgroup
  cg c;
  initial c = new(value);
endmodule
```

Replace `output` with `inout` for the second negative case. The clean `origin/main` install at `af89cfc50be1084cc86c48865f3f6ba78d4512fa` accepted and ran both forms in both editions without a diagnostic. The standalone legal-`ref` sampling behavior is tracked separately in [#448](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/issues/448).

## IEEE basis

IEEE Std 1800-2017 §19.3 and IEEE Std 1800-2023 §19.3 state that `output` or `inout` is illegal as a covergroup formal argument. See the official [2017 standard record](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/6700/) and [2023 standard record](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/7743/).

## Acceptance criteria

- Reject covergroup declarations with `output` or `inout` formals in strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Keep legal `input` and `ref` formals accepted, with live read-only `ref` sampling behavior covered under #448.
- Add registered positive and negative tests to the legacy and JSON runners, with exact diagnostics checked in both editions.

## Dependencies

None known.

## IEEE requirement

IEEE 1800-2017 and IEEE 1800-2023 Annex H §H.7.8 permits unpacked aggregate arguments for imported and exported DPI subroutines. Annex H §H.8.2 excludes open-array arguments from exports, but otherwise permits the same formal argument types as imports; fixed-size unpacked arrays are therefore legal. See the official [IEEE 1800-2017](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/6700/) and [IEEE 1800-2023](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/7743/) standard pages.

## Gap and evidence

The compiler drops an exported function with a legal fixed-size unpacked formal instead of generating a callable C stub. The current-main reducer `tests/negative/m10_dpi_export_fixed_array_argument.sv` reports that the fixed unpacked array argument is unsupported for DPI export. A compact reproducer is:

```systemverilog
module fixed_array_export;
  function int first_value(input int values[2]);
    return values[0];
  endfunction
  export "DPI-C" function first_value;
endmodule
```

On the existing current-main install, `iverilog -g2012 -o /tmp/ieee-census-export.vvp <reducer>` exits nonzero with the targeted “fixed unpacked array argument ... is not yet supported for DPI export; the export is dropped” diagnostic.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generate and link an export stub for legal fixed-size unpacked array formals in strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Use the correct direct-reference C ABI and preserve array shape, values, and input/output/inout copy semantics.
- Add an external C caller test covering at least a fixed-size integer array and a packed-element or multidimensional array, with round-trip checks for supported directions.
- Continue to reject exported open-array formals, which Annex H §H.8.2 prohibits.

## Dependencies

Extend the existing scalar and packed-vector export-stub path to fixed unpacked aggregate formals. This is independent of imported shortreal array support and must not relax the exported-open-array rejection.

## Gap

A wide unsigned index into a fixed string array is narrowed to a signed 64-bit address before the bounds check. Values such as `1 << 100` therefore alias element zero instead of returning the string default for an invalid read.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  string words[2] = '{"first", "second"};
  logic [127:0] index = 128'd1 << 100;
  string got;
  initial begin
    got = words[index];
    $display("got='%s'", got);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected `got=''`; the current string-load path narrows the address and can return `words[0]`. The paired 32-bit/100-bit index matrix and exact current path are recorded in [DD-029](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-029--wide-fixed-string-array-reads-alias-a-valid-element).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §7.4.6 requires the element-type default value for an invalid fixed-array read; an invalid wide index must not alias an in-range element.

## Acceptance

- Preserve full index width and signedness through bounds checking for string-array reads.
- Return the default string for out-of-range, negative, and unknown indices without reading or modifying an in-range element.
- Add paired 2017/2023 tests for 32-, 64-, and 128-bit signed/unsigned indices and neighboring valid indices.

## Dependencies

None known. Keep the string-array behavior separate from #414's packed bit-select bounds.

## Gap

Increment/decrement of a fixed unpacked-array element compiles but crashes VVP for integral arrays; real-array forms fail to update the element and index. The selected element must be updated once, and postfix must return its old value.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  int a[2] = '{5, 7};
  int idx = 0;
  int old_value;
  initial begin
    old_value = a[idx++]++;
    $display("idx=%0d a0=%0d a1=%0d old=%0d", idx, a[0], a[1], old_value);
  end
endmodule
```

## Gap

A part-select of a packed element can escape into a neighboring packed element when its base is out of range. A read returns the neighbor's bits rather than X, and a write changes the neighbor.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  logic [1:0][7:0] words = 16'ha520;
  integer pos = 8;
  initial begin
    words[0][pos +: 4] = 4'hf;
    $display("words=%h", words);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected value remains `16'ha520`; the recorded baseline produces `16'haf20`. A paired read reproducer returns `5` from a neighboring element instead of X. See [DD-022](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-022--packed-subpart-writes-escape-the-selected-element).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1 requires a wholly out-of-range part-select write to have no effect and a partial write to update only in-range bits; reads return X for out-of-range bits.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the bounds of every selected packed carrier for reads and blocking, compound, and nonblocking writes.
- Clip partially out-of-range writes to in-range bits and produce X only for out-of-range read bits.
- Preserve single evaluation of dynamic indices and ascending/descending declarations.
- Add paired tests before relaxing the separate mixed-driver rejection in DD-021.

## Dependencies

Prerequisite for #471. This is distinct from #414's multidimensional bit-select alias case.

## Gap

Two-state packed reads can return X for invalid selectors, and X bits from a partially out-of-range part-select can survive assignment into a two-state variable. The standard requires 0 for invalid bit-selects on two-state values and converts X/Z to 0 when assigning to a two-state destination.

## Reproducers

```systemverilog
module t;
  bit [7:0] value = '1;
  integer index = 8;
  initial $display("bit_oob=%b", value[index]);
endmodule
```

The current one-dimensional Icarus path prints `bit_oob=x`; IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1 requires `0` for this two-state value.

A separate paired reducer in DD-087 uses `bit [99:0] bv = '1; integer b = 96; bit [7:0] br = bv[b +: 8];`. The current result retains `xxxx1111` in `br`; the missing part-select bits must convert to zero on assignment, producing `00001111`.

IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023 §11.5.1 specify invalid bit-select results by source state and require partially out-of-range part-select reads to return X for out-of-range bits. §6.11.2 requires X/Z to become zero when converted to a two-state type.

## Acceptance

- Return 0 for invalid bit-selects on two-state packed values, including unknown and out-of-range indices.
- Convert missing X bits from partially out-of-range part-select reads to zero when the destination is two-state.
- Keep four-state result rules and in-range ascending/descending selections unchanged; add paired 2017/2023 focused cases.
- Record the tested limits in the packed-select matrix.

## Dependencies

None known. This tracks the two-state result/conversion rules and is separate from #414's multidimensional four-state alias and index-boundary case.

See [DD-087](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-087--out-of-range-part-select-of-a-two-state-vector-leaves-x-in-a-two-state-variable) for the paired reducer and logs.

## Gap

Plain escaped macro identifiers are rejected in conditional-compilation directives, although the directive grammar accepts a `text_macro_identifier`, which is a SystemVerilog identifier. The current preprocessor reports `` `ifdef without a macro name`` for the escaped name.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
`define \foo 1
`ifdef \foo
module escaped_macro_found; endmodule
`else
`error escaped_macro_not_recognized
`endif
```

IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5 Syntax 22-5 uses `text_macro_identifier` for conditional directives; §5.6 includes escaped identifiers in the SystemVerilog identifier grammar. IEEE 1800-2023 §22.5 likewise defines `text_macro_identifier` as a SystemVerilog identifier, and §5.6 includes escaped identifiers.

## Acceptance

- Accept escaped macro identifiers in `ifdef`, `ifndef`, and `elsif` in both strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Add self-authored defined/undefined, branch-selection, and escaped-identifier terminator cases to the preprocessor regressions.
- Preserve existing simple-identifier and macro-expansion behavior; malformed/unterminated escaped identifiers remain diagnostics.
- Record focused test evidence in the conformance matrix.

## Dependencies

None known.

## Scope

IEEE language support only. This is separate from issue #460, which tracks parenthesized Boolean expressions in conditional directives.

## Gap

A function returning an unpacked-array typedef is rejected when used as the subarray value in a nested unpacked-array assignment pattern. The compiler rejects a legal array-valued expression even though direct whole-array function-result assignment works. Implement the nested value path and keep malformed forms as ordinary source diagnostics.

## Current-state probe

Self-authored reducer:

```systemverilog
typedef int pair_t[2];
typedef pair_t pairs_t[2];
function automatic pair_t make_pair(input int base);
  make_pair = '{base, base + 1};
endfunction
pairs_t got;
initial got = '{make_pair(11), make_pair(21)};
```

On clean `origin/main` `af89cfc50be1084cc86c48865f3f6ba78d4512fa` (macOS ARM64), the nested form fails in both `-g2017` and `-g2023` with two elaboration errors: `Expression make_pair(...) is not compatible with this context. Expected array or array-like expression.` It does not ICE. The direct control `pair_t got; got = make_pair(11);` compiles and runs in both editions, printing `got=11,12`. This confirms the reported behavior on the clean baseline. The out-of-tree build used Homebrew Bison 3.8.2 plus explicit libffi/Z3 include and library paths; macOS's default Bison 2.3 fails at `parse.y:2236` before building, which is a local toolchain mismatch rather than a source failure.

The source path is confirmed on clean main. In `PEAssignPattern::elaborate_expr_uarray_()` (`elab_expr.cc`), nested items recurse for `PEAssignPattern` and `PEString`; `PEConcat` and `PEIdent` have dedicated diagnostics; any other non-null child, including a function call, receives the generic incompatible-context error. In VVP, `draw_array_pattern()` (`tgt-vvp/stmt_assign.c`) recurses only for nested `IVL_EX_ARRAY_PATTERN` nodes and otherwise evaluates a leaf according to the target element base type. Whole-RHS unpacked-array function calls take a separate `show_stmt_assign()` path to `draw_ufunc_uarray()` (`tgt-vvp/draw_ufunc.c`), so nested array-return values have no corresponding lowering path. The reproducer therefore reaches a missing elaboration case first, with a second required lowering path for the returned array value.

The older conformance note that direct whole-array function-return assignment is still a graceful `sorry` is stale: the clean-main control compiles and runs in both editions. Correct the matrix to distinguish that supported direct assignment from the still-failing nested pattern form.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023 §§10.9.1 and 13.4.1. §10.9.1 specifies that array-pattern items are evaluated in the context of assignment to the corresponding element type, with braces matching array dimensions; §13.4.1 allows nonvoid function results in assignments and expressions. The relevant wording is materially the same in both editions.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce the nested-form rejection and direct whole-array control on clean `origin/main` before editing.
- Add self-authored positive, negative, and boundary regressions for nested array-valued function results; register them in both the legacy and JSON runners for each applicable edition.
- Verify and cite the exact IEEE text, then update the clause matrix to correct the stale whole-array-return note and record the tested nested-form boundary.

## Current status — 2026-09-14

**Open: native null-input crash reproduced.** Audited against main `9c8f716b1` and its unchanged UVM pin `78c06547a2a0a29b3dc9dcafae62b75b2ff61544`.

The [pinned helper](https://github.com/accellera-official/uvm-core/blob/78c06547a2a0a29b3dc9dcafae62b75b2ff61544/src/dpi/uvm_regex.cc#L240-L290) calls `strlen(re)` before the null check when `deglob == 0`. The [Icarus DPI umbrella](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/uvm_dpi/uvm_dpi_iverilog.cc#L37-L75) still includes that helper. Its `regcomp` wrapper cannot intercept the earlier `strlen` call. Guards in the separate legacy regex entry points do not fix this path.

## Reproduction

A native C++ test of the unmodified pinned `uvm_regex.cc` on macOS produced:

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `uvm_re_comp(nullptr, 0)` | SIGSEGV (subprocess return code -11) |
| `uvm_re_comp(nullptr, 1)` | Returns null normally (control process exits 0) |

Minimal test:

```cpp
#include "uvm_regex.cc"
int main(int argc, char**) {
    regex_t* result = uvm_re_comp(nullptr, argc > 1);
    if (result) { uvm_re_free(result); return 2; }
    return 0;
}
```

Compile with C++ at `-O0`, the pinned UVM DPI include directory, and installed Icarus headers. On macOS, supply the usual `malloc.h` shim containing `#include <stdlib.h>`. Run without an argument for the crash, and with an argument for the control. Disable core dumps. Tested helper SHA-256: `1109dcc03d008f7124021bc271130a4edd35a34b5950372f48746f446445a61a`.

This reproduces the **native helper boundary**, not an SV-to-DPI null-string path. Reachability through ordinary SystemVerilog string arguments remains unverified. No remote exploit or memory overwrite is claimed.

## Closure requirements

1. Reject null before any length, indexing, or copy operation in the affected native entry path.
2. Add a permanent native regression with the null-regex failure and null-glob control; retain valid and invalid-pattern behavior. Separately establish SV/DPI reachability if claiming a simulator-triggered crash.
3. Review the diagnostic `sprintf` calls for bounded formatting. The original warnings are a hardening concern; the inspected fixed diagnostic messages do not demonstrate a buffer overflow.
4. Preserve the unmodified-UVM policy: use an appropriate upstream dependency update or a reviewed fork-owned boundary fix, rather than an untracked submodule edit. Do not substitute successful regex results for rejected input.

Related but distinct source-only regex edge cases are tracked as [DD-016](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-016--regex-edge-cases-during-legacy-abi-comparison); this audit does not claim they were reproduced or fixed.

## History

Originally reported from a macOS real-DPI build on 2026-08-10 at the same UVM pin. The September 14 audit confirms the null-regex defect remains; no simulator implementation was changed during issue cleanup.

## FIXED in commit `9f3666d` — m7 now passes

`m7_objection_stress_test` now ends at t=80 and passes; the full UVM suite
is **209 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (m7 un-skipped, KNOWN_FAIL now
empty). ivtest gate: 44 expected, 0 new, 0 stale.

### Root cause (recap)

A reference to `this` (or an enclosing automatic) from a detached
(join_none) fork body nested inside another detached fork resolved to null
for later loop iterations: the forked thread's inherited automatic-context
chain stopped linking back to the owning activation frame across frame
reuse, so `vthread_get_rd_context_item_scoped` walked wt/rd/owned/stacked,
matched nothing for the target scope, and returned a null item. In UVM's
phase hopper this made per-phase `drop_objection` run with `this == null`,
so `get_objection()` returned null and `drop_objection()` silently no-op'd
on the null handle — two phase-hopper objections never dropped and
`run_phases` never returned from `wait_for_objection(UVM_ALL_DROPPED)`.

### Fix

Strictly-additive last-resort fallback in
`vthread_get_rd_context_item_scoped` (`vvp/vthread.cc`): reached only after
every chain walk has already failed (i.e. the read would otherwise be
null), so it cannot alter any currently-resolving case. When the target
automatic scope has exactly one live activation there is no ambiguity, so
it resolves to that activation. Recursive scopes (>1 live context) stay on
the null path.

Regression test: `ivtest/ivltests/sv_this_nested_detached_fork.v`.
Reproducer kept at
`docs/conformance/repros/m7_this_null_nested_detached_fork.sv`.

### Out of scope (separate, pre-existing)

A loop-local captured by a *general inline* detached fork body (not `this`,
and not a task-call argument — #102 handles that) resolves to the scope's
single live frame, i.e. its last value rather than the per-iteration value.
That is a #102-class limitation, not a regression (it was null before), and
would need the general spawn-time closure capture #102 deliberately scoped
out. `this` is unaffected because a non-recursive method has a single live
activation.

## Fixed in commit `9f1909b` — and NOT the cause of m7

**The fork-capture bug is real and now fixed**, but the earlier claim that
it causes `m7_objection_stress_test` was WRONG. Correcting the record.

### The bug (fixed)

A single-branch `fork task(<automatic>); join_none` re-executed each loop
iteration evaluated the call arguments when the *detached* thread was
scheduled, not at spawn, so inside a class method (single activation
frame) every worker read the loop automatic's final value. IEEE
1800-2017 §9.3.2 requires the value at spawn.

### The fix (correct approach)

The naive "give the loop-body block its own frame" from the first
investigation regresses outer-automatic access (single-task-frame model),
so it was abandoned. The landed fix instead **hoists the callee `%alloc`
+ argument stores to run in the spawning thread, immediately before the
child's `%fork`** (`tgt-vvp/vvp_process.c` `show_stmt_fork` +
`fork_child_hoist_split_`). The callee frame is allocated before the
detach exactly as the fork thread's own frame already is, and the binding
is captured at `%fork` time. Guarded to join_none, single-branch, and the
exact wrapped-auto-call shape, so no other fork form changes.

declaration initializer (`fork automatic uvm_phase phase = ph; begin
process_phase(phase); drop_objection(phase); end join_none`), and that
form **already captured correctly** at baseline (a fork-scope automatic
initialized from an outer var gets per-spawn storage). Confirmed with a
reduced repro. The m7 workers' `fork worker(phase, idx); join_none` *was*
subject to this bug, but only mis-timed `idx` (all fired at t=80); the
objection *counts* stayed balanced. With the fix applied, m7 still fails
identically (`t=9200`), so the phase-hopper objection off-by-two on
`uvm_top` (27 raises / 25 drops) is a **separate, still-unidentified
issue**, not fork capture. Tracked separately; the m7 KNOWN_FAIL comment

## Not a bug — correct static-initialization ordering

On re-investigation this is **correct SystemVerilog behavior**, not a
defect. My reproducer conflated static-initialization order with a copy
failure.

`C e = new c;` where `e` is a *static* variable (the default) is a static
variable initializer. Per IEEE 1800-2017 §6.21, static initializers run
**before time zero**, before any `initial`/`always` process executes. In
the reproducer, `c.n = 42` (or `c.f()`) is a *procedural* statement that
runs at time 0. So the static initializer `new c` copies `c` while `c.n`
is still 0 — the pre-write value — which is exactly what a conforming
simulator does. iverilog even warns: "Static variable initialization
requires explicit lifetime in this context."

The netlist is correct: the `<shallow_copy>` node carries `c` as its
source operand; it simply executes in the static-init phase.

Verification — making the initializer procedural (an `automatic` variable
or a variable inside an automatic task) copies the post-write value as
expected:

```systemverilog
task automatic run();
  C c = new; c.n = 42;
  begin C e = new c; $display("%0d", e.n); end   // prints 42 (automatic → procedural init)
endtask
```

```
auto decl n=42
```

The statement form `d = new c;` also runs procedurally and copies 42.
Both correct. Closing as not-planned (invalid). The #100 fix and its
test are unaffected — the test already uses the procedural statement form.
title: Copy constructor as a declaration initializer (`C d = new src;`) does not copy

## Context

With per-instance class events now correct (PR #96), the UVM objection front door no longer cross-wakes. This un-masks a separate, pre-existing gap in objection **count** propagation that the shared-event cross-wake had been hiding.

## Symptom

`tests/m7_objection_stress_test.sv` (8 concurrent workers holding the run-phase objection until t=80, plus a child with an explicit count) against unmodified UVM 2020.3.1:

- The objection **counters** pass (`workers=8 child_drops=3`).
- But the run does **not** end at t=80 — it extends to the UVM 9200 s watchdog, so the end-of-sim time check fails.

The test completes (no wall-clock hang); it is on the harness `KNOWN_FAIL` list for this reason.

## Root cause (instrumented)

The `uvm_phase_hopper`'s `phase_hopper_objection` is raised on `uvm_phase` keys (`try_put` → `raise_objection(phase, ...)`) and the hopper waits on `wait_for_objection(UVM_ALL_DROPPED)` = `wait_for(UVM_ALL_DROPPED, uvm_root)`.

Instrumenting `uvm_objection::all_dropped` and `wait_for` shows, for the `phase_hopper_objection` instance:

```
DBG WAIT all_dropped objn=<hopper> key=uvm_root
DBG all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=<component_1> exists=0
DBG all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=<component_2> exists=0
...            (many component/phase keys)
# but NEVER: all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=uvm_root
```

So the hopper objection's `all_dropped` fires for every component/phase key as they drop, but is **never called for `uvm_root`** — its integer `m_total_count[uvm_root]` never returns to 0. Therefore the hopper's `@(m_events[uvm_root].all_dropped)` never wakes, `run_phases` never returns, and phasing only ends at the watchdog.

In the shared-event baseline this was masked: a *different* objection instance's `all_dropped` trigger cross-woke the hopper's waiter (1 trigger → 2 wakes), so the phase advanced anyway (prematurely — which is why the post-run function phases were documented as never executing).

## Expected behavior

When all phases have been processed and their hopper objections dropped, `phase_hopper_objection`'s `uvm_root` count reaches 0, `all_dropped(uvm_root)` fires, `run_phases` returns, and the run ends cleanly (≈ t=80 in this test), with the post-run function phases (extract/check/report/final) executing.

## Likely subsystem

UVM objection count propagation to `m_top` for a `uvm_phase`-keyed objection — `m_propagate` / `m_drop` / `m_forked_drain` climbing the hierarchy from a non-component key up to `uvm_root`. Needs a reduced pure-SV reproducer of the phase-keyed propagation to isolate whether a drop is lost or the climb terminates early.

## Severity

P0 (UVM semantic blocker) — this is the remaining blocker for full extract/check/report/final phase execution in M7.

## Related

- PR #96 (per-instance class events) fixes the language-level half.
- `docs/conformance/session_logs/2026-07-21_per_instance_class_events.md` has the instrumented evidence.
- `docs/conformance/m7_stress_findings_2026-07-18.md` (Finding 1) documents the original masked behavior.
title: UVM phase_hopper_objection never all-drops to the top under concurrent objection traffic (blocks clean run_phase completion)

```
ivl: t-dll-api.cc:817: ivl_variable_type_t ivl_expr_value(ivl_expr_t): Assertion `net' failed.
```

Legal SystemVerilog: assign `5` to the `id` property of the object held in `arr[0]`. Should compile and run, printing `5`.

8 (classes) / 7.4 (unpacked arrays) — property lvalue of an array-of-handles element.

tgt-vvp code generation. Backtrace:

```
#7  ivl_expr_value (net=0x0) at t-dll-api.cc:817
#8  draw_eval_expr_into_integer (expr=0x0, ix=4) at eval_expr.c:298
#9  show_stmt_assign_sig_cobject (net=...) at stmt_assign.c:2472
#10 show_stmt_assign (net=...) at stmt_assign.c:2514
```

P1 — compiler crash on legal SystemVerilog.

Pre-existing; discovered while testing per-instance class events (PR #96), but entirely unrelated to events — the reproducer above uses no events. 4. Use the measurements to decide whether a concrete optimization ticket is warranted. Close this assessment with evidence if no actionable bottleneck remains; otherwise link a narrowly scoped follow-up with its measured target and correctness gates.

## Summary

`seq_item_port.try_next_item(req)` falls through to the `uvm_sqr_if_base::try_next_item` error stub instead of dispatching virtually to the sequencer's override:

```
UVM_ERROR @ ... [try_next_item] Sequencer interface task not implemented
```

`tl_host_driver::a_channel_thread` calls `seq_item_port.try_next_item(req)` to non-blockingly check the sequencer for items. - The sequencer is `uvm_sequencer #(REQ, RSP)` extending `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` (defines `try_next_item` via the `UVM_SEQ_ITEM_PULL_IMP` macro)

## Summary

`wait(<vif-chain-expr>)` doesn't trigger when the underlying virtual-interface signal changes, because `nex_input` on a `NetEProperty` chain returns the root `this` nexus rather than the iface signal.

## Repro

`tests/wait_vif_isunknown_test.sv` (in the dev-branch test suite) — a `Watcher` class with `virtual my_if vif`, calling `wait(!\$isunknown(vif.rst_n))`. The wait never fires even after the testbench drives `iface.rst_n = 1`.

```sv
class Watcher;
  virtual my_if vif;
  task watch();
    wait(!\$isunknown(vif.rst_n));   // <-- never wakes
  endtask
endclass
```

## OpenTitan impact

`tl_monitor::monitor_reset` in OT uses:
```sv
wait(!\$isunknown(cfg.vif.rst_n));
forever wait(cfg.vif.rst_n != !cfg.in_reset);
```

Both block forever. `cfg.in_reset` stays stuck at 1 from time 0, every `tl_host_driver` request goes down the abort path, and `csr_wr` returns `UVM_NOT_OK`. Worked around in OT fork via `@(cfg.vif.rst_n)` edge events (see opentitan iverilog-uvm branch commit 3416154).

## Root cause

Pinpointed in `iverilog/net_nex_input.cc:171-174`:
```cpp
if (const NetExpr*base = get_base()) {
    delete result;
    result = base->nex_input();
}
```

For a chain like `vif.rst_n` (`NetEProperty(rst_n) over NetEProperty(vif) over NetESignal(this)`), recursion through `get_base()` reduces the result to the `this` nexus — the class handle, which never changes. The wait probe is therefore connected to a never-changing nexus and the wait while-loop never re-evaluates.

## Existing infrastructure

- The `%wait/vif/anyedge` runtime opcode exists (`vthread.cc:13843, of_WAIT_VIF_ANYEDGE`). It pops a vif, gets its anyedge functor, and registers the thread on the wait list. This is what `@(vif.sig)` already uses.
- `NetEvProbe::set_vif_anyedge(N, M, pre_N)` is the netlist-level marker. `tgt-vvp/vvp_process.c:1723` consumes it and emits `%wait/vif/anyedge`.
- The path is fully wired for `@(vif edge)` events. The gap is `wait()`-loop elaboration: it builds a `NetWhile(cond, NetEvWait(NetEvent))` where `NetEvent` is signal-driven, not vif-aware.

## Suggested approach

Make `PEventStatement::elaborate_wait` (elaborate.cc:7397) detect when the wait expression contains a virtual-interface signal chain. When it does, replace the standard `NetEvWait(signal-driven NetEvent)` with a `NetEvWait` whose probe carries `set_vif_anyedge(N, M, pre_N)`. ## Status

The OpenTitan UART DV testbench now **compiles to a VVP file with 0 elaboration errors and 0 code-generation errors** (using `-DSYNTHESIS` + `-DUVM_NO_DPI`). The simulation runs but hits runtime errors that prevent UVM test execution from completing.

## What was fixed to get to zero compile errors

- Complex event expressions in auto tasks → SV-mode `continue` (compile-progress)
- `NetEScope` used as event expression (clocking block) → caught and skipped
- `NetEProperty::synthesize()` → silent null override (prevents double error count)
- Empty event wait (`wa->nevents()==0`) → `set_t0_trigger()` for non-auto, return body for auto
- NB assignment in function → actually create `NetAssign` (blocking) in SV mode
- `elab_lval.cc` compile-progress path → return null instead of invalid nested lval
- `stmt_assign.c` compound string assignment assert → compile-progress skip
- `eval_expr.c` wide-constant assert → truncate-to-zero fallback
- `draw_net_input.c` uwire multi-driver error → downgrade to warning (treat as TRI)
- `vpi/sys_icarus.c` → add real `$system()` implementation

## Runtime errors (blocking test execution)

### 1. `$value$plusargs` with class property / constant args

The most frequent blocker. OpenTitan DV passes class properties or string constants as the destination argument:

```
ERROR: dv_lib/dv_base_test.sv:79:   $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiConstant.
ERROR: dv_lib/dv_base_test.sv:91:   $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: alert_esc_agent.sv:63:       $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: cip_base_vseq.sv:469:        $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: dv_report_server.sv:17:      $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
```

**Fix needed**: In `vpi/sys_vcsuser.c` `$value$plusargs` implementation — accept `vpiClassVar` destination using `vpi_put_value()`, and silently skip (no match) for `vpiConstant`.

### 2. `$sformatf` type 116 (class object)

```
ERROR: cip_base_scoreboard.sv:589: $sformatf does not support argument type (116).
```

Type 116 = `vpiClassObj`. When `%0s` or `%p` is used with a class handle, the formatter falls through with no handler.

**Fix needed**: In `vpi/sys_display.c` — add a case for `vpiClassObj` that emits `<object:0xADDR>` or calls the object's `convert2string()` if available.

### 3. Unresolved functor stubs

```
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfcba9c20_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd2a4920_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd4132e0_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd453dd0_0; created placeholder net
unresolved vpi name lookup: v0x60bbfd54fb50_0; using null handle
```

These are likely struct/packed-array output ports on RTL modules (TL-UL signals) whose synthesis emitted stub labels that weren't resolved. The VPI handle lookup then gets a null.

**Fix needed**: Investigate which RTL struct ports produce these stubs; may require fixing packed struct output port synthesis in `draw_net_input.c` or `vvp_process.c`.

### 4. Callf async warning (secondary)

```
Warning: callf child did not end synchronously (caller=uvm_pkg::_ivl_276.m_register_pair callee=...get); caller entering join wait
```

UVM internal pair registration hits the async callf path. Non-fatal but indicates a phase-execution gap.

## Suggested fix priority

1. `$value$plusargs` vpiClassVar — most frequent, blocks build phase config
2. `$value$plusargs` vpiConstant — silently no-op
3. `$sformatf` type 116 — formatting only
4. Unresolved functor stubs — RTL investigation needed

## Reproduction

```sh
ulimit -v 3000000
# compile (0 errors)
iverilog -g2012 -DSYNTHESIS -DUVM_NO_DPI \
  -I accellera-official.uvm-core/src \
  -I opentitan/hw/ip/uart/dv/env \
  ... (full dep list in memory/project_opentitan_uart.md) \
  -o /tmp/uart_dv.vvp \
  accellera-official.uvm-core/src/uvm_pkg.sv \
  ... (RTL + DV files)
# run (shows runtime errors)
vvp /tmp/uart_dv.vvp
```

## Summary

Two pre-existing TLM failures that prevent real driver/sequence testbenches from working:

### 1. Sequencer/driver handshake (`seq_trace_test.sv`)

`seq_item_port.get_next_item(item)` spins infinitely with `UVM_ERROR [get_next_item] Sequencer interface task not implemented`.

The port's `m_if` (set during `resolve_bindings`) is either null or not resolved to the correct IMP. Virtual dispatch on `m_if.get_next_item()` falls to the `uvm_sqr_if_base` base class stub, which returns immediately — causing the driver loop to spin forever.

The `tlm_debug_test` (blocking_put_port) works correctly, so basic TLM port dispatch is functional. The issue is specific to `uvm_seq_item_pull_port` / `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` — the parameterized sequencer IMP combination. The IMP's `get_next_item` at `TD_uvm_pkg._ivl_341.get_next_item` exists in the VVP but is never dispatched to.

### 2. Analysis port subscriber write (`analysis_test.sv`)

`ap.write(t)` in a monitor does not reach the subscriber's `write(t)` method. The same `m_if` / TLM resolve_bindings issue likely applies to `uvm_analysis_port`.

## Root cause hypothesis

`uvm_port_base::resolve_bindings()` does not correctly populate `m_imp_list` for the parameterized sequencer IMP, leaving `m_if = null`. Without a valid `m_if`, the virtual dispatch in `get_next_item` reads null from `@` and falls to the base class stub.

The `uvm_blocking_put_port` works because its IMP registration path is simpler (no 3-level parameterization with `this_type`).

## Investigation notes

- VVP label `TD_uvm_pkg._ivl_341.get_next_item` exists — the IMP implementation is compiled correctly
- The `connect()` call in `connect_phase` appears to reach the IMP (property 58 of `sqr`)
- Dispatch trace (`IVL_VDISPATCH_TRACE=1`) shows the failure happens before `run_phase` can be reached in 2-second window
- Pre-Phase-3 binary and pre-Phase-3 VVP both fail identically — confirmed pre-existing

## Files to investigate

- `vvp/vthread.cc` — `maybe_dispatch_virtual_method_call_`, look for why `m_if` is null
- `vvp/vvp_cobject.cc` — associative map (`Mo`) property access for `m_imp_list`
- `accellera-official.uvm-core/src/base/uvm_port_base.svh` — `resolve_bindings`, `m_add_list`, `set_if`

## Blocks

This blocks all real driver/sequence testbenches. Should be fixed before Phase 4 (register layer), which requires a working sequencer.
